newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil changes method to calculate GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil changes method to calculate GDP.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank has changed its method for calculating gross domestic product in dollars which raises GDP figures considerably, said Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economic department.

The new method, which translates GDP into dollars using average annual exchange rates instead of the theory of purchasing power parity, would lift GDP results for the first seven months of the year to $701 billion from $576 billion, Lopes said.
Lopes said that under the old method, the current account gap in the first nine months was 3 percent of GDP. Under the new method, the current account gap narrowed to 2.53 percent of GDP.

"We've been underestimating the value of gross domestic product," Lopes told reporters. He said the new method was used by most international and financial institutions and that by using it Brazil would bring its GDP calculations more in line with those of the market.
He said that under the new method, the 1995 GDP increased to $690 billion from $560 billion, and 1994 GDP to $553 billion from $528 billion.
Lopes said that the new "more common" method had become possible because of economic stability.
"Yes it results in an increase (of GDP)," he said.
According to a Central Bank statement, the 1995 current account deficit was 2.57 percent of GDP under the new system, compared with 3.17 percent under the old system.
